study_identification.title: Normative modelling of molecular-based functional circuits captures clinical heterogeneity transdiagnostically in psychiatric patients

study_characteristics.study_objective: To combine REACT (Receptor-Enriched Analysis of functional Connectivity by Targets) with normative modeling to create functional networks enriched with neurotransmitter systems and generate normative models of these networks to capture functional connectivity deviations in patients with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and ADHD.

hc_age.answer: CamCAN: Mean 52.3, SD 18.3; UCLA: Mean 31.2, SD 8.7

hc_sex.answer: CamCAN: M 255, F 241; UCLA: M 60, F 51

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: REACT toolbox (version 0.1.7); PCNtoolkit (version 0.27); FSL PALM; Python (SciPy, statsmodels, sklearn)

quality_checking_detail.answer: Participants with incomplete demographic or psychometric data were excluded.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) with site (UCLA, Cambridge) as a random effect.

predictor_effects.answer: Site: random effect; Age/Sex: fixed effects.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study used a hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) approach to model site effects as a random effect, which explicitly handles this nuisance variable.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: We chose to utilise a hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) approach which can accommodate signal and noise variance in data from multiple sites by estimating different but connected mean and variance components through shared prior distributions across sites. ... Specifically, we used site (UCLA, Cambridge) as a random effect as well as age and sex as fixed effects, resulting in normative regional molecular-enrichedFCvarianceanduncertainty.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study used a 70/30 train-test split on the healthy control data to validate the normative models.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: Normative models were trained on 70% of the healthy control data across both UCLA and CamCAN datasets and tested on the remaining 30%.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.location: Results, Modelling the normative molecular-enriched brain

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study does not mention using a separate, independent dataset from the same domain for validation.

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The normative models, trained on healthy controls, were applied to clinical cohorts (schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, ADHD) to calculate deviation scores. This represents validation on a different domain.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: Predictions using these models were also made for the clinical cohorts, where age and sex were used to predict their molecular-enriched networks. This provides both point estimates as well as measures of predictive confidence, allowing us to statistically quantify deviations from the normative molecular-enriched networks with regional specificity.

diseases_studied.answer: Schizophrenia (SCHZ); Bipolar Disorder (BPD); Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)

clinical_groups_age.answer: SCHZ: Mean 35.1, SD 8.8; BPD: Mean 34.6, SD 8.9; ADHD: Mean 32.2, SD 10.1

clinical_groups_sex.answer: SCHZ: M 32, F 6; BPD: M 24, F 22; ADHD: M 19, F 18

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: 1x4 ANOVAs, t-tests, binary logistic regression, correlation analyses.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study brings together normative modeling and molecular-enriched analyses to offer a potential path forward for both mechanistic elucidation as well as to help bring neuroimaging closer to clinical implementation.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Normative models of molecular-enriched networks captured functional connectivity deviations in patients with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and ADHD. Substantial overlap was seen in symptomatology and deviations from normality across groups, but these could be mapped into a common space linking constellations of symptoms through to underlying neurobiology transdiagnostically.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Group average molecular templates from separate subjects, moderate collinearity between some molecular-enriched networks, cross-sectional data, and relatively small clinical cohort sizes.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The integration of novel functional-molecular neuroimaging techniques, normative modelling, and a transdiagnostic perspective offers methodological and theoretical progress towards an understanding of the shared neurobiological foundations that underpin psychiatric conditions.

general_notes.general_notes: The study utilizes a novel method called REACT (Receptor-Enriched Analysis of functional Connectivity by Targets) to create functional networks enriched with neurotransmitter systems. This is a key methodological innovation. The molecular templates used were: NAT (10 healthy participants, M/F: 6/4, mean age 33.3), DAT (30 healthy subjects), SERT (16 healthy individuals, M/F: 10/6, mean age 59.4), VAChT (6 healthy participants, 3 male, 3 female, mean age 67.0), GABA-A (6 healthy individuals, male = 6, female = 0, mean age 43), and mGluR5 (31 healthy individuals, male = 18, female = 13, mean age 45.3).
